questions.question: What character separates a CSS property from its corresponding value?
questions.explanation: A colon (:) separates the property name from its value in a CSS declaration.

questions.question: Which character must terminate every CSS declaration?
questions.explanation: Every CSS declaration must conclude with a semicolon (;) so the parser knows where the declaration ends.

questions.question: What is the only valid comment syntax in pure CSS stylesheets?
questions.explanation: CSS exclusively uses block comment syntax wrapped between /* and */.

questions.question: In the declaration margin: 10px 20px;, what does 20px represent?
questions.explanation: In 2-value margin shorthand, the first value is for top and bottom, and the second is for left and right.

questions.question: What happens if a browser encounters an unrecognized CSS property or syntax error?
options: It crashes the tab with an error banner
It silently ignores the invalid declaration and continues parsing the rest of the stylesheet
It reloads the page in safe mode
It converts all text to comic sans
questions.explanation: CSS is fault-tolerant; the browser parser simply skips invalid or unrecognized declarations and continues parsing.
